comments.author: @BTFranklin
comments.text:
Hey Wes, thanks for another informative video. You are definitely one of my favorite AI news creators and I appreciate it.

One suggestion I have for when you're doing various comparison tests is that you should always start a new thread/conversation/whatever when you start your new topic or question. The reason for that is because when you're submitting your next question, the entire conversation is being submitted as context, which can (should?) influence the answer you get, even if your next question seems unrelated.

Additionally, if you're doing a side-by-side comparison and one model has a new thread while the other has cruft from your earlier questions, it's not really an equivalent comparison. I see many people making this mistake when doing informal evaluations. It's important to think of the entire conversation as one unified request, every time you submit it.

Some might argue that the models need to be able to distinguish this themselves, and that's totally fair, but in an analytical comparison it's still something to consider for accuracy.

comments.author: @courtneyb75
comments.text:
The thought that open source will very likely eventually reach the level of AGI is, frankly, a bit unnerving. Think about it, if we get to that point, it's like opening Pandora's box. Suddenly, every bad actor out there gets their hands on what could be the most powerful tool known to humanity. It's not just about the technology itself, but about who controls it and how it's used. It's one thing for a company to develop advanced AI that's got some sort of controls in place, but ensuring open source is used ethically and responsibly? That's a whole different ball game. We need to tread carefully here, because once that genie is out of the bottle, there's no putting it back. 

Once AGI is achieved, that changes everything. It's the ultimate game changer. With AGI, suddenly you have the capability to crack any code, to breach any security system. This includes gaining access to the most guarded secrets, like nuclear weapon blueprints. The self-improvement capabilities of AGI mean it can refine, enhance, and outperform any existing technology, creating versions far superior to what we have now. Whoever gets their hands on AGI essentially becomes the most powerful individual on Earth. You could command AGI to generate a billion dollars in 24 hours, and it would be capable of infiltrating banking systems, executing complex financial maneuvers beyond our current understanding.

As a species, we're not ready for this. We're too immature, too reckless. Handing over such power to humanity in its current state is like giving a teenager a fighter jet. It's not just about the technological breakthrough; it's about the wisdom to use it. And we're definitely not there yet. 

Consider entities like ISIS and similar groups, who are antagonistic towards Western civilization, would jump at the chance to use AGI for their own ends. Their goals have been clear for decades – to target what they consider 'infidels.' Now, imagine them armed with AGI. It's not just about physical attacks anymore; it's about cyber warfare, financial destabilization, and spreading ideological propaganda at an unprecedented scale. AGI would give them the ability to orchestrate complex global campaigns, disrupt critical infrastructures, and perhaps even manipulate political landscapes. This isn't fear-mongering; it's a realistic assessment of what could happen if such power falls into the wrong hands. The potential for misuse is immense and could redefine global conflict.
